source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for Eczema / Dermatitis
source.publisher: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

sections.label: Signs That Need Urgent Medical Attention
items: Eczema with pus discharge, yellow crusting, or increasing warmth, this indicates a secondary bacterial infection
Widespread skin involvement with blistering or skin breakdown
Eczema associated with fever
Severe eczema covering large parts of the body that is not responding to any treatment

sections.label: Self-Care at Home
items: Apply a moisturiser immediately after bathing while the skin is still slightly damp, this is the most important step in managing eczema
Apply moisturiser multiple times during the day, not just once
Bathe daily with a mild soap and normal temperature water; avoid hot water
Keep fingernails short to reduce damage from scratching
Avoid scratching, scratching worsens eczema and risks infection
Identify and avoid triggers: specific soaps, detergents, fabrics, plants, or foods that make the skin worse
Wear loose, cotton clothing to reduce irritation
Avoid high-risk occupational exposures if possible: agricultural work, construction, hairdressing involve frequent skin contact with irritants
For contact dermatitis, identify and remove the cause (e.g. a specific soap, metal, or plant)
Atopic dermatitis is often worse in winter, extra moisturising is important in cold weather
Do not use any steroid creams on your own without a doctor's guidance, especially on the face or skin folds

sections.label: See a Doctor
items: Any new rash with redness, scaling, or itching that is not improving within a week of basic care
Eczema on the face, eyelids, or genitals
Rash that you suspect may be caused by an allergen or irritant at work
Eczema that keeps recurring in the same areas
Skin that has become thickened or leathery in patches from long-standing eczema
Eczema with signs of infection: pus, yellow crust, or increasing redness
Eczema in a child, particularly if involving the face, skin folds, or causing disturbed sleep from itching

sections.label: Refer to Higher Centre
items: Severe eczema not responding to treatment at the primary care level
Widespread disease requiring phototherapy or systemic treatment
Suspected allergic contact dermatitis where patch testing is needed to identify the allergen
Unusual presentations that may be mistaken for eczema: psoriasis, fungal infection, or cutaneous lymphoma

review.notes: All corticosteroid names, potency classifications, calcineurin inhibitor names, and systemic drug regimens excluded. Key safety message retained: do not self-apply steroid creams without medical guidance.
